facts.statement: payment's error spans for Charge carry the 'Invalid token' exception with loyalty_level=gold (20 traces, capped).
payment logs the Invalid-token message as warn 25 times between 19:39:18Z and 19:42:21Z; no error-level line exists in the window.
payment has only info logs before 19:39:18Z, with no Invalid-token warnings earlier.
In a failing trace, payment's charge span is the deepest error. Checkout's Charge client span and PlaceOrder carry the same message, and frontend returns 422.
checkout has no error logs and no Invalid-token lines of its own.
Feature flag paymentFailure is ENABLED at variant 50%, the only one of 18 flags switched on.
payment has one Deployment revision (created 19:11:23Z) and no warning events or restarts; checkout has one revision (19:11:22Z) and no warnings.
payment's Charge server errors are about 0.087/s, and its flagd client error rate is negligible; no failing dependency shows in payment's client spans.

checkout's 5m error ratio rose from 0.18 at 19:25 to about 0.95 at 19:29, driven by CurrencyService/Convert client errors that stop by about 19:29. Checkout's PaymentService/Charge client errors start at 19:40.
flagd produced no log lines in the window, so no flag-evaluation change is visible in its logs.

hypotheses.statement: The paymentFailure flag was switched to 50% at about 19:38-19:39Z and is the direct trigger of the Invalid-token failures.

hypotheses.statement: The failures are limited to gold-loyalty users, because the trace sample was capped and every sampled error is gold.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check currency's own server spans and error logs for 19:25-19:29 and look for a config or deploy change there; do not blame currency from checkout's client spans alone.
hypotheses.statement: checkout's early 19:25-19:29 currency errors come from a separate fault in the currency service, now resolved; this is a secondary issue.

inferences.statement: payment is the origin of the current burn, and checkout's concurrent P1 is a downstream effect of payment's Charge errors.
No rollout or config deployment in payment or checkout preceded the onset, so the trigger is more likely a runtime flag or config change than a new image.

root_causes.cause: Charge handler fails token validation (Invalid token, gold-loyalty users seen so far) from about 19:39:18Z. Likely triggered by the enabled paymentFailure flag or a config/credential change, not by a rollout (single revision since 19:11).

diagnosis.summary: payment is failing about 30% of requests because its PaymentService/Charge handler rejects requests with 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. demo.user_context.loyalty_level=gold' starting at about 19:39:18Z. Checkout's payment-side errors and frontend's 422s carry that same message, so checkout is a victim of payment for the current burn. The trigger is not yet confirmed. The flag paymentFailure (ENABLED, 50%) is the leading candidate, but its enable time is unknown. Checkout's separate early errors (19:25-19:29, on CurrencyService/Convert) resolved before the payment onset and are not the current driver.

alternatives.why_not: payment and checkout each have one revision (19:11), with no earlier release before the onset, so there is nothing to roll back to that would remove the flag-driven failures.
No stuck or leaking process is evidenced: payment has no restarts or warning events, and the failures are deterministic token rejections, which a restart would not clear.
The errors are validation rejections, not a capacity shortfall, so more replicas would only spread the same failures.

plan.no_action_reason: The trigger is a feature flag (paymentFailure, ENABLED at 50%), which is outside the allowed actions. A human should check flagd's change history for who enabled it and when, then disable it or set it to off. Confirm that payment recovers and that checkout's PaymentService/Charge errors stop. Separately, check the currency service's 19:25-19:29 fault, which is a secondary issue.
plan.summary: No automated action is supported. payment's Invalid-token failures start at 19:39:18Z with a single Deployment revision since 19:11:23Z, so this is not a bad release, and the enabled paymentFailure flag (50%) is the likely trigger, which none of the allowed actions can change. A human should confirm the flag change and disable or revert paymentFailure in flagd; checkout's P1 should then recover as a downstream effect.

facts.statement: All 20 sampled failing checkout traces fail at checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge with 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. demo.user_context.loyalty_level=gold', then propagate to PlaceOrder, frontend (HTTP 422, gRPC 13) and frontend-proxy.
Payment logs show 25 warn entries with the same Invalid token exception (charge.js:48) between 19:39:18Z and 19:42:21Z. Checkout has no error-level logs in the window.
Checkout's client error series for PaymentService/Charge is about 0.081/s, matching checkout PlaceOrder server errors of about 0.081/s.
Payment's 5m server error ratio is 0.364, close to checkout's 0.371. Its Charge errors are the main server error series apart from checkout PlaceOrder.
Payment's error ratio first appears at 19:40:08Z (0.095) and rises to 0.395 by 19:42:38Z, so payment's errors start about 19:40Z.
The flag paymentFailure is ENABLED at variant 50% (value 0.5, targeting false) and is the only one of 18 flags that is on.
Payment and checkout have single revisions created at about 19:11Z, with no warnings. flagd's deployment is also unchanged, so no rollout explains the errors.
Checkout's 5m error ratio peaked at 1.0 near 19:28Z and returned to 0 by about 19:33Z, before payment's errors began.
Payment's p95 latency is about 1.9s for most of the window, with a single spike to 61.8s at 19:14.

hypotheses.statement: The paymentFailure flag was switched on at about 19:39-19:40Z, which would match the first payment errors. The flag state shows no change time.

hypotheses.statement: Payment's ~1.9s p95 plateau is a separate latency issue, possibly caused by the flag path or retries, and not part of the error cause.

inferences.statement: Checkout is the symptom, not the origin. Its errors are payment's Charge failures passed up the chain, and payment's errors begin before checkout's error rate reaches its current level.
The paymentFailure flag (50%) is the most likely trigger. A 50% failure rate applied to a share of checkouts fits the 31.75% checkout error ratio, and no rollout change explains it.

root_causes.cause: Payment's Charge handler fails about a third to a half of requests with 'Invalid token' for gold-tier users. The likely trigger is the flagd flag paymentFailure (ON at 50%), though that link is not yet proven.
The paymentFailure flag was switched on at 50% by a config change, not a flagd rollout. This is the candidate trigger for payment's failures, and its change time has not been established.

diagnosis.summary: Checkout's ErrorBudgetBurn (~31.75% 5m error ratio) is caused by failures in payment's Charge call. Every sampled failing checkout trace fails at PaymentService/Charge with 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. demo.user_context.loyalty_level=gold'. Payment's own server error ratio (0.364) matches checkout's, and payment's errors start around 19:40Z. Checkout only relays the error. The only live change is the flagd flag paymentFailure (ON, 50%), which plausibly explains the ~50% payment failure rate, but its change time is not confirmed and the 'Invalid token' message for gold users may be a separate payment bug. Payment is the service to fix. Checkout's earlier spike near 19:28Z and payment's ~1.9s p95 are unexplained.

alternatives.why_not: Payment and checkout each have one revision from about 19:11Z, before errors began at about 19:40Z, so there is no bad release to roll back to.
Errors are deterministic Invalid token failures in Charge for a share of requests, not a stuck or leaking process.
Failures are logic or flag-driven, not a capacity shortfall; more replicas would not reduce the error ratio.

plan.no_action_reason: No available action fixes this. The likely cause is flagd flag paymentFailure (ON at 50%), whose change time is unconfirmed. A human should check flagd change history and turn it OFF if confirmed. Payment owners should check gold-tier token validation at charge.js:48.
plan.summary: Checkout's errors are payment Charge failures relayed upstream, and payment's errors start about 19:40Z with no rollout change. No rollback, restart or scale would fix a flag-driven fault, so no actions are proposed and a human should verify and revert the paymentFailure flag.
